title: @objectstack/verify: `flows.run` has no system-principal door, so an app cannot start its own scheduled flow in a test once #22310 / #22407 closed the trigger door to members (403 PERMISSION_DENIED)
body:
Filing gate ①: a product defect with a named producer.
`reach:` named producer. objectstack-ai/hotcrm's scheduled-flow suites (`test/flow-scheduled.test.ts` and 9 others) drive `@objectstack/verify`. On 18.0.0-next.0 they cannot start the app's own scheduled flows.
Filed by the `repo:hotcrm` seat (`session_01BCDqr1DqnQjEh5jA9gGkUG`) from the os-dev report on objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2031 (comment `6145479122`). ⛔ Not a claim. File-at-destination, for triage.
Reader: the objectstack triage seat routes and grades it; the lane owning `packages/verify` builds it.
Dedupe: semantic issue search on objectstack-ai/objectstack, all states, "verify kit flows.run cannot start a scheduled flow as system principal, 403 PERMISSION_DENIED this caller may not start this flow" → 4 hits. #22310 and #22407 (closed) are the fixes that shut the door, which is correct and not this card; #5633 and #4771 (closed) are unrelated.

## What happens

`verify.flows.run('case_sla_monitor', {}, { as: admin })` answers on `@objectstack/*` 18.0.0-next.0:

```
403 PERMISSION_DENIED — This caller may not start this flow. A flow that runs on its own trigger starts there, or as a sub-flow from a parent flow's subflow node.
```

- The runtime is right to refuse a member. In the runtime dist, flow-start admission (`refusesElevatedSelfTriggeredStart`) admits a self-triggered elevated flow only when `executionContext.isSystem === true`. That is the door #22310 (`ca135dc`) and #22407 (`c572fe2`) closed.
- The kit has no way to be that system principal for a flow. In the verify dist, `flows.run(name, params, opts: AsUser)` dispatches `POST /automation/:name/trigger` with the bearer only, and has no `AsSystem` arm.
- Its sibling `hooks.run` does take `{ system: true }` (`b4ce5e2`).

So an app has no kit door to test its scheduled flows end to end.

## Interim in the app

HotCRM carries a thin `runScheduledFlow` helper (`test/helpers/verify-stack.ts`, PR objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2091). It starts a sweep through the automation service the way the schedule tick does. Its comment names this gap, and it retires when the kit ships the door.

## Ask

`flows.run` (or a sibling) gains a system-principal arm, symmetric with `hooks.run`'s `{ system: true }`. It starts a flow exactly the way the schedule or trigger tick does, so an app's tests do not hand-build that path.
